name: Kwinti
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Borges, Robert. 2014. The Life of Language: dynamics of language contact in Suriname. PhD, Radboud Univ. (contains Kwinti description; stress statement not verified)

sources.citation: Muysken, Pieter & Norval Smith (eds.). 2015. Surviving the Middle Passage: The West Africa-Surinam Sprachbund (Trends in Linguistics Studies and Monographs 275). Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton. Open access (OAPEN hdl 20.500.12657/24642). Esp. Smith, 'Sub-, super-, and adstrate phonology in creole languages', pp. 261ff.
sources.note: No statement about Kwinti stress. Kwinti appears only as accent-marked comparative forms in Table 3 p.277 (boló 'blow', golón 'ground', ga(l)ási 'glass', wáta 'water', síkísi 'six'), sourced to Huttar (1983 ms.) and Smith & Huttar (1984); p.88 groups Kwinti with Ndyuka/Aluku/Paramaccan as descendants of Plantation Sranan.

sources.citation: Borges, Robert. 2014 [copyright 2013]. The Life of Language: dynamics of language contact in Suriname. PhD dissertation, Radboud Universiteit Nijmegen (LOT Dissertation Series 348). Utrecht: LOT. Ch. 7 'Coppename Kwinti: the influence of adstrate languages on a Surinamese creole', pp. 181-214.
sources.note: Nothing on Kwinti word stress. Only phonological remark (p.190): Kwinti 'lacks the tonal complexities and implosive obstruents of Saramaccan, and has five contrastive vowels as opposed to seven'; sec. 5 treats /r/ variation, 'pikin' pronunciation, tags, negation, Dutch elements. (The stress/tone passage on pp.55-56 concerns the Kumanti ritual language, not Kwinti.)
Nothing on stress; bibliography pointers only (Borges 2014, van der Elst 1975, Hoogbergen 1992).

sources.citation: Huttar, George L. 1988. Notes on Kwinti, a creole of Central Suriname (Society for Caribbean Linguistics Occasional Paper 20). St. Augustine, Trinidad: Society for Caribbean Linguistics. 16 pp. OCLC 702389267.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only dedicated linguistic description of Kwinti (SIL fieldworker, Bitagron 1982 data; source of the ASJP list and of the accent-marked forms in Smith 2015). If any published sentence states Kwinti stress/tone placement, it is here.

sources.note: Comprehensive historical phonology of all Surinam creoles including Kwinti (Glottolog cites it for Kwinti subclassification); discusses reflexes of English stressed syllables and accent/tone in the Maroon creoles and may characterise Kwinti prosody.
